senses.sense_definition: The circular rotating platform of a record player, or a record player itself.

examples.text: She carefully placed the vinyl record on the <w>turntable</w> and lowered the needle.
The club DJ adjusted the speed on the <w>turntable</w> before transitioning to the next track.

senses.sense_definition: A circular platform that rotates around a central axis.

examples.text: The display case featured a rotating <w>turntable</w> to show the statue from every angle.
Food heats more evenly because the microwave includes an interior <w>turntable</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A large rotating platform installed in a circular pit, used to turn railway locomotives and cars onto different tracks.

examples.text: The historic steam engine was brought onto the railway <w>turntable</w> to face the opposite direction.
Workers monitored the circular pit as the massive <w>turntable</w> slowly aligned with the siding.

senses.sense_definition: To manipulate sound and create music using DJ equipment; to scratch or perform turntablism.

examples.text: He spent years practicing before he started <w>turntabling</w> live in front of huge crowds.
The guest musician began <w>turntabling</w> during the middle of the hip hop track.

senses.sense_definition: To play a record or track using a turntable.

examples.text: The radio host is known for <w>turntabling</w> rare jazz albums from the sixties.
That classic single was frequently <w>turntabled</w> at underground clubs all summer.

senses.sense_definition: To rotate, pivot, or spin around, or to cause something to turn as if placed on a revolving platform.

examples.text: The dancer kept <w>turntabling</w> smoothly across the polished floor during the routine.
The old train cars were mechanically <w>turntabled</w> inside the repair shed.
